changes.before: Assyria is the ancient template for the second. In the seventh century BCE it was the most effective war machine in the world — a standing army, siege engineering, the administrative capacity to deport whole populations. It won very nearly every war it fought. And the way it sustained that machine was to institutionalize terror: its own inscriptions record what it did to cities that resisted, and those records were part of the deterrent apparatus. After Nineveh fell in 612 BCE, the empire vanished within a generation, leaving almost nothing behind — not merely the regime, but its continuity as a civilization.
changes.after: Assyria is the ancient template for the second. In the seventh century BCE it was the most effective war machine in the world — a standing army, siege engineering, the administrative capacity to deport whole populations. It won very nearly every war it fought. And the way it sustained that machine was to institutionalize terror: its own inscriptions record what it did to cities that resisted, and those records were part of the deterrent apparatus. After Nineveh fell in 612 BCE, the empire soon collapsed. But Assyrian society and culture continued after the empire; the end of a regime cannot be equated with the disappearance of an entire civilization.
changes.author_intent: 保留军事胜绩不保证政权延续的例子及短句收束；将覆亡的帝国与继续存在的亚述社会文化分开，不把政治崩溃说成文明灭绝。

changes.before: Assyria won nearly all its wars. What it lost was itself.
changes.after: The Assyrian empire won nearly all its wars. What it lost was the empire itself.
changes.author_intent: 保留军事胜绩不保证政权延续的例子及短句收束；将覆亡的帝国与继续存在的亚述社会文化分开，不把政治崩溃说成文明灭绝。

changes.before: But look across three centuries. Sparta left almost no philosophy, drama, architecture, mathematics, or historiography — while Athens in the same period left work humanity is still using. More fatally, the Spartan citizen body kept shrinking across those centuries, until by the fourth century BCE there were too few to fill its own phalanx, and its institutions were too rigid to admit new citizens. In the end nobody destroyed Sparta. It contracted out of existence.
changes.after: But look across three centuries. In the philosophical, dramatic, mathematical and historical works and architectural remains that survive today, Sparta's legacy is far less rich than Athens's — while Athens in the same period left work humanity is still using. More fatally, the Spartan citizen body had long been shrinking, and by the fourth century BCE there was a serious shortage of citizen soldiers, while its institutions made admitting new citizens difficult. In 371 BCE Sparta suffered a major military defeat at Leuctra; internal contraction and external defeat together weakened its hegemony. Sparta continued to play a role in the Hellenistic age. It did not disappear from history.
changes.author_intent: 保留长期备战、公民人口收缩与制度僵硬的分析；文化比较仅及留存材料，承认留克特拉军事失败及其后延续，不以内部收缩抹去军事史。

changes.before: Spain and the Netherlands in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries are the cleanest demonstration of this. Spain had American silver, the finest infantry formations in Europe, and an empire spanning two hemispheres. The Netherlands was a strip of low ground that had just pulled free of it, with a fraction of the population and no natural resources.
changes.after: Spain and the Netherlands in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries can serve as a limited illustration of this claim. Spain had American silver, the finest infantry formations in Europe, and an empire spanning two hemispheres. The Netherlands was a strip of low ground gradually gaining its independence through resistance to Spanish rule, with a fraction of Spain's population and limited natural resources, but with economic supports of its own, including peat and fisheries.
changes.author_intent: 保留西荷对照的节奏、人物和涵育分析，将其限定为例证；补清荷兰独立过程和资源，分开1559年有限求学禁令与1609至1614年驱逐，收窄印刷业和地区断言。

changes.before: A century later the Dutch had the Amsterdam exchange, Leeuwenhoek's microscopes, Rembrandt and Vermeer, Grotius and Spinoza, and the printing industry of the whole continent — Descartes moved there to write his books, because there they could be printed. Spain in the same century forbade students from studying abroad, systematically expelled several hundred thousand Moriscos who formed the backbone of its southern agriculture and crafts, and institutionalized censorship.
changes.after: By the seventeenth century the Dutch had the Amsterdam exchange, Leeuwenhoek's microscopes, Rembrandt and Vermeer, Grotius and Spinoza, and had become a major European centre of printing and publishing — Descartes moved there to write his books, because there they could be printed. Spain had restricted its Castilian subjects' study abroad as early as 1559, though with exceptions; from 1609 to 1614 it also systematically expelled several hundred thousand Moriscos, an important part of agriculture and crafts in Valencia, Aragon and other regions. Censorship of thought was institutionalized there too.
changes.author_intent: 保留西荷对照的节奏、人物和涵育分析，将其限定为例证；补清荷兰独立过程和资源，分开1559年有限求学禁令与1609至1614年驱逐，收窄印刷业和地区断言。

changes.before: The Chinese imperial edict of 127 BCE known as the Order of Extended Grace is the cleanest demonstration. The decree announced that a vassal king's fief would no longer pass intact to the eldest son of his principal wife, but be divided among all his sons.
changes.after: The Chinese imperial edict of 127 BCE known as the Order of Extended Grace is the cleanest demonstration. The central government's decree permitted vassal kings to request the allocation of part of their fiefs to their sons and younger relatives, with the emperor approving their enfeoffment as marquises.
changes.author_intent: 保留阳谋、皇权推动削藩的政治压力和公开安排的实质强制。请求与准许不等于现代意义的自由选择；仅去掉所有儿子必须分封、任何封地必然碎化及诸侯无一例外不能拒绝的史实过强断言。

changes.before: Not one word was hidden. Everyone could see this was a policy for dissolving the vassal states — within a few generations, any fief would be split into fragments too small to threaten anything. And not a single vassal king could refuse, because refusing meant telling all of his own sons, to their faces, that they did not deserve a share. The decree moved the pressure off the axis between the center and the kings, and onto the axis between each king and his own children.
changes.after: Not one word was hidden. Everyone could see this was a policy for weakening the vassal powers — as fiefs were subdivided again and again, the land and power at each king's disposal would shrink. But under imperial authority, permission can carry the weight of a command, and a request does not mean a free choice without cost: refusal carried political costs, and a king might also have to explain to sons and younger relatives expecting a grant why he would not give them a share. The decree drew pressure from the axis between the centre and the kings onto the axis between each king and his own sons and younger relatives.
changes.author_intent: 保留阳谋、皇权推动削藩的政治压力和公开安排的实质强制。请求与准许不等于现代意义的自由选择；仅去掉所有儿子必须分封、任何封地必然碎化及诸侯无一例外不能拒绝的史实过强断言。

changes.before: In 1919, the defeated state took no part in the negotiations, the treaty was delivered for signature in the form of an ultimatum, and one clause required it to acknowledge in the text its full responsibility for the war.
changes.after: In 1919, the defeated state took no part in the negotiations, and the treaty was delivered for signature in the form of an ultimatum. Article 231 required Germany to accept that Germany and its allies were responsible for the loss and damage caused to the Allied powers and their nationals by the war arising from their aggression. This reparations clause was also widely understood as a judgement of war guilt, becoming an important source of humiliation for the defeated party.
changes.author_intent: 准确交代第231条对德国及其盟国的损失损害责任；保留战争罪责解读和羞辱感的历史后果，分开条文与政治效果，不改相邻段落的非单因果限定。
